ReadTrack Architecture and Core Principles
ReadTrack is designed as a local-first mobile document reader and reading tracker for Android and iOS devices. The primary goal is to provide readers with an interactive, private, and distraction-free environment where every document remains entirely on their device. There is no mandatory cloud connection, no account registration requirement, and no remote server tracking reading behavior.

The underlying technology relies on Tauri 2, combining a robust Rust core with a modern TypeScript frontend. The Rust backend handles sandboxed document storage, cryptographic deduplication using BLAKE3 hashing, normalized abstract syntax tree generation, SQLite persistence with full-text search indexing, and a state machine tracking user dwell times across reading segments. The React frontend presents a responsive mobile interface with virtualized rendering and smooth navigation. Inter-process communication bridges the layers through typed serialization commands.

Tracking reading progress accurately requires dividing documents into small, manageable units called reading segments. For rich text formats such as Markdown and Plain Text, consecutive semantic blocks within each section are grouped together. Segments maintain a target word count between forty and two hundred twenty words while strictly respecting section boundaries and breaking at headings. Each segment begins in an unread state and transitions to reading and read as the user spends sufficient dwell time within the active viewport reading zone. Calculations remain isolated within individual sections to guarantee consistent reading speeds.

By keeping all business logic inside Rust services and maintaining SQLite as the single source of truth, ReadTrack ensures deterministic behavior and crash resilience. If the mobile operating system suspends or closes the application, the reader state can be restored seamlessly to the exact paragraph, block, and character offset where the user paused. All user annotations, bookmarks, reading milestones, and historical logs remain fully preserved locally across consecutive application sessions without external synchronization.
